visualContract.layoutPolicy: SidebarProvider has a real wrapper and separate desktop/mobile state; useSidebar is context, not DOM. Desktop source widths 16rem/3rem are bound through the public style override to semantic tokens; native 255px inner+border and 48px collapsed examples remain evidence. Mobile uses source 18rem preferred Sheet width capped to viewport clearance; its data-slot is sidebar, so generic SheetContent slot rules alone do not style it. Source hardcoded hidden default Close is retained and target supplies a real visible SheetClose inside navigation content. Desktop physical left/right container, gap, icon/offcanvas state and mobile modal ownership remain distinct. Pinned Sidebar consumes dir but forwards it only to mobile SheetContent; the reference keeps the provider layout LTR for physical gap order and explicitly sets dir on Header/Content/Footer/Inset text regions. Right desktop inner border faces content. Native menu 8px corner role is retained;32/28/48 button sizes, group inset/captions, badges/actions/submenus and skeleton geometry are explicit bounded reference roles. Collapsed labels may be visually hidden only when each icon link has a persistent aria-label; optional Tooltip is supplementary, not sole naming. The reference composes Rail only on desktop; mobile has real Trigger/Close controls. Source Shortcut Ctrl/Meta+B still intercepts even editable descendants; preventDefault on SidebarTrigger callback does not cancel its subsequent internal toggle. Controlled desktop callback can be ignored while source cookie still records the requested state; no new cancellable event is invented. Mobile open state is independent, and the source 767px breakpoint is retained. Source variants/API stay in CEM/UX; no fixed native page height/position or source-id anatomy remains.
